name: Variable Phase Order
description: A mechanic where the sequence of game phases or types of actions available in a round is not fixed but can change from round to round. This change might be determined by player choices (e.g., a rotating 'leader' player chooses the phase order), random draws, or conditions met in the game. It requires players to be adaptable and can significantly alter strategic considerations each round.

parameters.name: Determination Method
parameters.description: How is the phase order for a round determined (e.g., player vote, role selection, card draw, dice roll, rotating chairman).
parameters.default_value: Role selection by players in turn order

parameters.name: Available Phases/Actions
parameters.description: The set of possible phases or action types that can be ordered (e.g., Income, Movement, Build, Combat).

parameters.name: Impact of Order
parameters.description: How significantly does the order of phases affect gameplay and player strategies? Are there strong synergies or anti-synergies based on order?
parameters.default_value: Significant impact, as earlier phases can enable or restrict options in later phases.

parameters.name: Frequency of Change
parameters.description: Does the phase order change every round, or less frequently based on specific triggers?

examples_in_games.specific_implementation_notes: Players select roles (phases) in turn order. The selected roles are executed for all players, but the selecting player gets a privilege. This effectively creates a variable phase order each round based on player choices.

examples_in_games.game_name: Race for the Galaxy / San Juan
examples_in_games.specific_implementation_notes: Players simultaneously and secretly choose a phase they want to occur. All chosen phases happen, with bonuses for those who selected them. The set of active phases varies each round.
Players choose strategy cards in turn order. The order in which these strategy cards are typically resolved (by initiative value on the card) defines a significant part of the round's flow.
Certain game actions are selected by players (like 'Engineer' or 'Urbanization') which then become available phases for the round, often in a player-determined or bid-for order.

notes_on_combination_modification: Variable phase order adds a significant layer of strategic depth and replayability. Players must constantly evaluate which phases are most beneficial to occur early or late in a round, and how their opponents' choices will affect them. It can be complex to manage if there are too many possible phases or if the determination method is too chaotic.
